reuse.why: Reuses getWorstCaseAmount and the matching tolerance getApproxNumberThreshold, and routes getScheduledAmount through the new function, but adds getExpectedAmount as a near-synonym of the existing getScheduledAmount instead of extending it.

duplication.why: Call sites keep their own 'amount == null ? 0 : …' dispatch that getScheduledAmount already handles, and the budget template keeps its own isbetween/isapprox gate in front of a function that already handles every operator.

placement.why: The approximate worst case is defined in shared/schedules.ts next to the ranged worst case, where amount resolution lives.

scope.why: Limited to the amount rule, its server consumers, tests and a release note.

maintainability.why: Two public amount resolvers (getScheduledAmount and getExpectedAmount) with optional loosely typed op, and consumers such as the API's expectedAmount and the client balance still call getScheduledAmount without the operator, so they silently keep the exact value.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList decides by itself which operators go through getExpectedAmount; server/api-models.ts expectedAmount and desktop-client Balance.tsx call getScheduledAmount without the operator, so the new rule never reaches them.

disguised_duplication.where: No copied block; the leftover duplication (per-site null dispatch, template operator gate) is open, not disguised.

one_place.where: The rule is defined once in getExpectedAmount (shared/schedules.ts), but schedule-template.ts gates it with its own operator check and api-models.ts expectedAmount and the client Balance call getScheduledAmount without op, so not every path applying the expected amount gets the approximate worst case.
